resources.string: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, and draw your legs gently toward your chest.
Lie back and raise one leg. Hold behind the thigh and gently draw it toward you, keeping the knee softly straight.
Sit tall with the soles of your feet together. Let your knees relax outward without pushing them down.
Step the named leg back, keep that knee straight without locking it, and its heel down. Bend the front knee gently. Use a stable wall or railing if needed.
Hold a stable wall or railing. Bend the named knee and gently bring that heel toward your bottom, keeping knees close. Skip if support is unavailable or balance feels difficult.
Kneel in a split stance, gently tuck your pelvis, and keep your spine neutral as you shift forward.
Place the named heel a short step forward with toes up. Bend the other knee and hinge gently at the hips with a long back; rest hands on the bent thigh.
Step the named leg back, keep its heel down, and soften both knees. Stay upright and use a stable wall or railing if you need balance.
Stand with both feet grounded. Bring the named arm across your chest and gently support it above or below the elbow; keep the shoulder relaxed.
Stand tall, draw your shoulders gently down and back, and lift your chest slightly without arching your lower back.
Reach both arms forward with hands together. Gently round your upper back and let your shoulder blades move apart; keep your knees soft.
Raise one arm and bend the elbow so your hand rests behind your head. Rest the other hand above that elbow and apply only gentle pressure; keep your ribs relaxed.
Place both hands on a fixed, sturdy surface around waist height. Step back and hinge at your hips, keeping your back long. Skip if suitable support is unavailable.
Stand beside a wall. Reach both hands toward it and gently lean your hips away until you feel a mild stretch along your side. Keep both feet grounded.
Place one forearm against a wall with the elbow at shoulder height. Turn your chest gently away until you feel a mild stretch. Keep the shoulder relaxed; do not force the turn.
Add at least one posture to continue.
